## Wheel failures: observed vs coverage
- Build cause: the existing release build action defaults to CPython 3.11 and the bindings do not enable abi3, yielding cp311-cp311 wheels. That fixed-version ABI is why a 3.14 binary-wheel resolver cannot use them. Enabling abi3 is the fix; building six separate version-specific wheels is not required. A fixed build interpreter remains valid when the emitted ABI floor/tag is correct.
- #611 reports a concrete pip download sc-compose==1.6.1 --python-version 3.14 --only-binary=:all: resolution failure; published artifacts were cp311-cp311, not abi3: https://github.com/randlee/sc-compose/issues/611 .
- #611 reports a locally built 1.7.0 extension failing import on one macOS 27 / arm64 / Homebrew Python 3.14.7 setup; the later correction explicitly leaves linker/loader root cause unconfirmed: https://github.com/randlee/sc-compose/issues/611#issuecomment-6344556681 . Published cp311 wheel import was reported working in Python 3.11.13.
- #820 reports installer rejection/PATH-dependent selection when host Python differs from the existing 3.11 requirement, motivating a >=3.9 wheel contract: https://github.com/randlee/sc-compose/issues/820 .
The 4 platforms x CPython 3.9-3.14 = 24 cells, each pip+uv, are a user-approved compatibility PROCEDURE covering all three packages per cell, NOT 24 reproduced failures or a mandatory preflight/publish gate. This plan edit did not rerun those historical reproductions. Intel macOS/Windows ARM wheel gaps in #611 remain triage candidates, not added release targets.

## Parallel execution and file ownership
After U.1, dispatch U.2/U.3/U.6/U.7 concurrently; D1-D7 are approved, and the selected-base handoff remains the authorized writer's L1 action. U.6 owns only generator/CLI docs/site files and uses existing dependencies, not Cargo.lock. U.7 owns binding sources/manifests and Cargo.lock, no root lint/CI files. U.8 follows U.7 ABI code and owns the dispatch-only wheel procedure/workflow and its normal evidence; U.9 wires only the small artifact-consuming CI test, never a matrix preflight or publish gate. U.9 consumes the producer contracts to wire shared Justfile/CI/installer inputs once; U.5 also installs the supported sc-publish /prerelease kit. No matrix-to-preflight or publish-assignment verification interface exists. This is why U.6 and U.7 have no dependency on one another or U.5.
Upgrade critical path5 remains; appended user-required U.9->U.10->U.11->U.12->U.13 makes full planned critical path9, width4,13 sprints. This added serial chain is the user's explicit after-upgrades/last-fuzz sequence, not an invented documentation-to-ABI dependency. Shared paths always have a real dependency path, not a fabricated serial edge between unrelated features. No U.6->U.7 documentation-to-ABI edge or required throwaway 0.8.4 cross success.

## Evidence lifetime — sole owner (E1-E3)

Reuse same-head evidence; changed code/configuration or failures justify reruns. If existing retention expires first, retain the needed artifact through existing CI controls or rerun the affected exact-candidate build/checks and use the new actual hashes, never reconstruct a certificate. Use existing CI artifact-retention policy; after final acceptance stop actively maintaining verification summaries and let scratch/log artifacts expire normally. No new evidence service, manual matrix database, duplicate proof certificate or committed reports/**. Persistent regression tests and shipped docs are product assets, not temporary evidence.
E3. For EVERY real-bd exercise in U.10-U.13 use one isolated throwaway bd/Dolt instance at a time, never the shared server on port3308; the lead coordinates exclusive use across runners. Remove disposable local-index services/environments, baseline-suite overlays and temporary build/install worktrees after results are captured, on success or failure. Keep only ordinary CI results/hash links needed for the actual acceptance; no baseline fork or ongoing rehearsal infrastructure. The private rehearsal never uploads to PyPI/TestPyPI.

## Sanity / scope

D1-D7 are explicitly user-approved with the named implementation owners; pending implementation is not a reopened policy decision. Flaky tests are redesigned with controlled inputs, not sleeps/races/load. The user now authorizes review/fix iterations until no issues remain, followed by independent quality-mgr review. This does not create permanent review machinery. Earlier exact-head approvals cover their reviewed revisions only.
